part.company: Velankani Information Systems Pvt. Ltd., Bangalore, India
part.notes: Verify material grade and obtain MTC before production

drawing_requirements.internal_corner_radius: Not specified on drawing — confirm permissible radius with designer

process_sequence.name: Raw material preparation
actions: Check bar for bow and twist
Mark both components with individual identification numbers

process_sequence.name: Rough milling — rectangular body
process_sequence.machine: Universal milling machine (VISPL-TLR-001) or Vertical ram precision milling machine (VISPL-TLR-003)
sequence: Mill first broad face — establish datum A
Flip and mill opposite broad face parallel
Mill one side square to datum A
process_sequence.caution: Machine opposite faces alternately to reduce bending. Avoid heavy vice clamping — bowed bar springs back after release.

process_sequence.name: Stabilisation and straightness check
actions: Allow parts to cool completely after rough milling
Leave overnight if production time allows
Check bow on surface plate with dial indicator
process_sequence.note: Formal stress-relieving heat treatment normally unnecessary for MS but may be needed if material repeatedly distorts

process_sequence.name: Finish surface grinding
process_sequence.machine: Perfect surface grinding machine 1000×500 mm travel (VISPL-TLR-014)

method: Place datum face on magnetic chuck
Flip component several times during finishing
Light cuts ~0.005–0.01 mm near final size
thickness_20mm.check: Measure at both ends and centre — no taper or centre-high/centre-low

method: Use side supports and magnetic blocks
Flip component to avoid grinding a curve
width_30mm.note: Grinding preferred over precision milling for reliable parallelism

process_sequence.name: Finish overall length
method: Hold finished ground faces in soft jaws or on protected parallels
Set that face as length datum
process_sequence.check: End squareness against ground broad face

process_sequence.name: Machine end profile — two recesses
reason_for_wedm: Only 0.01 mm total tolerance on end features
Both recesses produced accurately in one setup
Cut passes through full 30 mm width
Internal corner radius much smaller than end mill
No start hole needed — recesses open to outside edges
wedm_setup: Use finished end face as longitudinal datum
Use ground top and bottom faces as vertical datums
Support 410 mm bar along its length
Allow only required end portion to overhang fixture
Verify bar fits safely in machine tank and fixture
process_sequence.wedm_cuts: One rough cut + minimum one (preferably two) skim cuts. Apply final wire offset from trial measurement.

alternative_method_milling.cutter: 8 mm side-and-face cutter or slotting cutter
steps: Finish top recess with bar supported flat
Control both shoulders independently using DRO
Rough to ~4.8 mm depth, finish in light passes
Machine bottom recess using same datum system
alternative_method_milling.warning: Do not assume cutter width equals 10.000 mm. Every component needs in-process gauging with gauge blocks or high-resolution height gauge. WEDM remains the safer route.
alternative_method_milling.internal_corner_radius_note: Milling leaves radius equal to cutter radius — confirm acceptable with mating component before using VMC

vmc_backup.corner_radius_left: ~R3 with 6 mm end mill, ~R1.5 with 3 mm end mill — confirm with designer

process_sequence.name: Chamfering and deburring
process_sequence.method: Milling chamfer cutter or careful hand deburring
actions: Do not round over accurately machined shoulders
Do not create large chamfer on measuring datums
Remove all loose WEDM slugs and burrs
process_sequence.note: For internal step edges — confirm if full 0.5 mm chamfer required or only a small burr break

machine_allocation.equipment: Universal mill (VISPL-TLR-001) or Vertical ram mill (VISPL-TLR-003)

rectangular_body.equipment: Vernier or height gauge on surface plate

rectangular_body.positions: Both ends, centre, two positions across width

rectangular_body.equipment: Surface plate and dial test indicator
Surface plate, slip gauges and dial indicator

end_profile.note: Calipers are NOT adequate for 0.01 mm tolerance
equipment: Toolmaker's microscope, CMM or profile projector (preferred)
Calibrated height gauge with gauge blocks on surface plate
Outside micrometer for central 10 mm web
Gauge blocks and dial comparator for shoulder positions
end_profile.instruction: Record actual values — do not only write OK

drawing_clarifications.description: End view implies 10 mm central web with ~5 mm removal from both top and bottom. Drawing does not explicitly state symmetry. Confirm with designer.

Recess corners drawn sharp but no permissible radius specified. WEDM leaves a small radius ~equal to wire radius. VMC milling leaves R1.5–R3 depending on cutter. Confirm acceptable radius with mating component designer.

route_summary: Cut 32×22 MS stock to 415 mm → rough mill to ~410.4×30.2×20.2 mm → stabilise → surface-grind to 30.000×19.995 mm → finish mill length to 410.00 mm → WEDM two end recesses with skim cuts → apply 0.5×45° chamfers → deburr, demagnetise and inspect
